subject: Post-call: technical sync & JSON validation / retry plan for Acumen integration
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Schultz <anna@acumen-analytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: technical sync & next steps (SDK/auth/reranker/JSON)

Anna — thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

What we covered (high level)
- Integration surface: SDK bootstrapping + recommended auth (API key for PoC, OIDC + mTLS for production)
- Request routing: per-route model pinning (low-latency vs cost tier), region affinity for GDPR data, automatic fallback to quantized variant
- Structured output: you outlined needing a strict JSON contract for downstream ingestion (order object + line_items array + status field)
- Robustness: constrained decoding (schema-first, token-beam checks), validation + deterministic retry semantics, and a soft-fail path for partial parses
- Embeddings & reranker: two-stage (lightweight embed + rerank) to keep inference cost predictable; caching top-k vectors per user session

Action items we agreed on
1) Acumen: share a small sample payload and a prioritized list of fields you must have vs optional (you said ~50 records).
2) Redwood (Marissa / Dev): propose a JSON schema + validation strategy and a retry semantics doc for partial/invalid responses.
3) Schedule a 60-minute technical design review next week to lock the schema and routing policy.

Attachments: I’ve included a short post-call notes PDF and an initial sketch of the schema (redwood-json-schema-v2.json) — both attached for reference.

Question for you: for the PoC, do you prefer an API-key-based sandbox or should we prepare an OIDC flow from day one? For timeline, you mentioned internal approvals next Wednesday — if we can get the sample payload by EOD Monday, we’ll draft the schema EOD Tuesday.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: technical sync & next steps (SDK/auth/reranker/JSON)

Thanks, Sergio — helpful recap. We’re aligned on most points. Quick clarifications from our engineering side: 

- Sample payload: attached (acumen-sample-payload.json) — contains 25 representative orders, and we’ve flagged mandatory fields (order_id, customer_id, total_cents, line_items[].sku, line_items[].qty, status).
- PoC auth: API key is fine for the sandbox. For production we need OIDC + SCIM for team provisioning; SRE will validate mTLS options later.
- Partial output handling: critical. We cannot block downstream ingestion on truncated or malformed JSON. Prefer that the response include an explicit "parse_status" (ok | partial | failed), and a "parse_errors" array for diagnostics. If parse_status != ok, payload should include a best-effort "raw_text" + a best-effort "structured" object.

We can get you the 50-record set by Monday EOD. Also looping in our SRE lead offline if you need firewall / peering info for a staging endpoint.

Thanks — Anna
Anna Schultz
Head of Platform Integrations | Acumen Analytics
anna@acumen-analytics.com

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Schultz <anna@acumen-analytics.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2026 11:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: technical sync & next steps (SDK/auth/reranker/JSON)

Anna — thanks for the sample. I looked through the 25 records and a few quick thoughts / concrete proposal for validation + retry semantics: 

1) Schema-first approach- We will formalize a JSON Schema (attached: redwood-json-schema-v2.json) and run server-side validation on generated output before returning to you. Validation outcomes: 
   - valid: full structured object returned, parse_status = "ok"
   - minor_issues: structured object returned with parse_warnings array, parse_status = "partial"
   - invalid: include parse_errors and raw_text, parse_status = "failed"

2) Constrained decoding (model-side)- Use schema-guided token constraints at generation time (field names / enumerations allowed set) + beam-filter stage. This reduces common truncation or hallucinated fields. We’ll enforce max token limits per field and apply a post-gen JSON reparsing pass.

3) Retry semantics- For requests that return parse_status != "ok":
   - Immediate transparent retry (1 attempt) with nudge to decoding temperature and stricter token constraints.
   - If retry still fails, return parse_status = "partial" with best_effort_structured and a stable request_id so you can request a synchronous re-process later.
   - Explicit idempotency: include client_request_id header to make retries idempotent on our side.

4) SDK primitives- We’ll add helpers in the JS/Python SDK to:
   - validateAgainstSchema(payload) -> returns standardized parse_status / parse_errors
   - autoRetryAndNormalize(req, opts) -> applies retry rules above and returns normalized structured object or the raw_text + diagnostics

5) Observability- Expose token-level timing + a per-request validation summary to the Console (so you can set alerts on partial/failed parse ratio).

Attached is a short reference snippet (in the schema file) and a suggested default retry policy we can tune. Happy to walk this through in the design review.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev@redwood.ai

Thanks Anna and Dev — great progress. To summarize and lock the plan before the design review (proposed Tue 2026-09-07 10:00 PT):

1) Deliverables before the review (due Mon EOD):
   - Acumen: full 50-record sample data set (you confirmed EOD Monday)
   - Redwood: finalized JSON Schema (v2 -> v3 candidate), validation matrix, and default retry policy (Dev will produce)
   - Logistics: a sandbox API key for Acumen and a shared Drive folder with the spec (link below)

2) Design review agenda (60 mins):
   - 10m: goals & success criteria for PoC
   - 20m: schema walkthrough + required vs optional fields
   - 15m: constrained decoding + retry semantics (Dev)
   - 10m: embeddings + reranker architecture (Marissa)
   - 5m: next steps & acceptance criteria for PoC

3) Acceptance criteria (PoC) — proposed
   - >= 95% parse_status == ok on the 50-record sample within our default timeout
   - End-to-end latency SLO: 500ms median / 1.5s p95 for structured responses during PoC load
   - Clear audit record per request (validation outcome + token usage)

Please confirm the proposed review time or suggest alternatives. I’ve added the HubSpot deal and a Drive spec link above, and will create a sandbox API key once we have the sample set.

Best,
